title: Security review: Encryption & KMS/BYOK/HSM - Aurora Bank
summary: Aurora Bank ran a security deep-dive with Redwood focusing on encryption at rest/in transit, BYOK flows, HSM-backed keys, audit logging, and compliance artifacts. Customer requires HSM-backed key control, EU data residency for a subset of workloads, and immutable audit export to their SIEM. Redwood covered envelope encryption, KMS integrations, private deployment options, and next steps for a BYOK demo and attestation docs.

Ravi to prepare BYOK demo runbook and sample API calls - due 2026-07-15

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Maya (Aurora Head of Security), Luis (Aurora Cloud Architect), Erin (Aurora Legal), Jake (Platform)

Summary (auto): Security deep-dive on encryption and key management. Customer leaning toward BYOK with HSM-backed keys, wants attestations, audit log export, and EU residency for PII data. Discussed envelope encryption, key wrapping, ephemeral keys, and private deployment options.

[00:00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Uh, quick intros - I'm Jamie Lin, I'm the AE on the account, with Ravi and Sofia from the technical team.
[00:00:12] Maya: Hi, I'm Maya, Head of Security at Aurora. We've got Luis, Erin and Jake on as well. Thanks for running through this, we've got some pretty strict KMS and HSM requirements so we wanted to make sure redwood's approach lines up.
[00:00:26] Ravi: Great, thanks Maya. High level we want to cover encryption at rest and in transit, BYOK flows, HSM support and audit logging. We'll also touch on deployment options and compliance artifacts like SOC 2 and ISO certs.
[00:00:40] Luis: Sounds good. One quick note, we are EU-first for a subset of PII workloads - so data residency and key location matter.
[00:00:50] Sofia: Thanks, we'll call that out as we go. Quick starter question - Aurora, when you say BYOK what does your ideal flow look like? Do you want to manage keys in your cloud KMS and grant Redwood access, or have Redwood import keys into an HSM under your control, or an EKM-style remote key server?
[00:01:10] Maya: Preferably we keep keys in our KMS. We use AWS KMS for most workloads, and for high-risk data we use an HSM-backed key store with FIPS 140-2 L3 requirements. We want key material that we manage and rotate, with evidence that Redwood cannot access the unwrapped key.
[00:01:28] Jamie: Understood. Redwood supports envelope encryption and customers can bring keys from common cloud KMS providers. For HSM-grade controls we support both HSM-backed keys via cloud provider KMS integrations and also on-prem HSM or partner HSM integrations for Private deployments.
[00:01:46] Ravi: To add detail, our common pattern is envelope encryption: customer-managed master key (CMK) is used to wrap and unwrap a data encryption key (DEK). The DEK is used by the runtime to encrypt model artifacts and persisted caches. We do not store the plaintext CMK; only wrapped keys are stored.
[00:02:05] Luis: So the CMK never leaves our KMS in plaintext?
[00:02:08] Ravi: Correct. For the BYOK flow, Redwood calls your KMS to perform Encrypt/Decrypt or GenerateDataKey calls. The unwrapped DEK exists in memory only for the operation and is cached in secure memory for the KV cache TTL, and we have mechanisms to clear it.
[00:02:27] Jake: Do you support EKM where our HSM is called via network for wrap/unwrap on every operation, or is it only an initial key import?
[00:02:36] Sofia: We support both patterns depending on deployment. For Hosted customers we typically use the cloud KMS integration where we invoke Encrypt/Decrypt per wrap/unwrap or GenerateDataKey and keep strict audit trails. For Dedicated or Private deployments we can support an EKM-style remote HSM or direct HSM appliance where each operation routes to the customer's HSM.
[00:02:55] Maya: Okay, so auditability is critical for us. We need immutable audit logs for all key usage and admin changes and the ability to stream those logs to our SIEM. How granular are Redwood's audit logs?
[00:03:09] Ravi: Good question. We log key wrapper operations, API calls that reference CMKs, admin policy changes, role assignments, and we capture the caller (principal), timestamp, operation, and request IDs. Logs are tamper-evident, rolled to WORM storage, and we can forward them via syslog or an S3 export to your SIEM. There's also support for push to cloud-native log services.
[00:03:30] Erin: From a legal/compliance perspective we need attestations — SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — and proof that keys are HSM-backed where claimed. Can you provide certs and HSM model/attestation?
[00:03:42] Jamie: Absolutely. We'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. For HSMs we provide architecture docs showing HSM vendor, model and that encryption operations are performed by HSM or HSM-backed KMS. For Dedicated/Private we can work with your team to provide remote attestation or connector details.
[00:04:00] Luis: Is there support for hardware-backed key attestation (e.g. TPM or HSM attestation tokens)?
[00:04:06] Ravi: We can support HSM attestation flows; in cloud KMS cases the cloud provider exposes attestation and key origin metadata. For on-prem HSMs we can support vendor-specific attestation and if required we can do an architecture review with the HSM vendor.
[00:04:19] Maya: How about key rotation and compromise scenarios? We have strict rotation windows and require clear rollback/compromise playbooks. If a CMK is revoked, do you have re-keying and re-encryption support?
[00:04:30] Sofia: Yes. We support versioned keys and key rotation. For DEKs we can rewrap with a new CMK; for stored artifacts we follow a re-encryption pipeline where we can re-encrypt persisted data or fall back to previous key versions depending on the data class. We'll collaborate on a runbook for revocation and rotate-on-read where feasible.
[00:04:50] Jake: Will re-encryption require downtime? Our SLAs are tight for some routes.
[00:04:55] Ravi: Usually you can do gradual rewrap and lazy re-encryption to avoid downtime — rotate keys and rewrap on first access, with background batch jobs to catch cold data. For high-sensitivity items we can schedule maintenance windows.
[00:05:08] Maya: About encryption in transit — do you use TLS? mutual TLS? How are mTLS certificates managed?
[00:05:15] Jamie: All traffic to the Redwood hosted API is TLS 1.2/1.3 and we support mTLS for private peering and Dedicated connections. Certificate rotation is automated for our side; for mutual TLS we'll accept client certs from Aurora and can integrate with your PKI for cert provisioning.
[00:05:31] Luis: Data residency: we need EU-only data at rest for PII. Can you ensure certain customer datasets and their keys stay in eu-central-1 and never replicate outside?
[00:05:41] Sofia: Yes, we have region pinning and data residency controls. For hosted we can pin storage and KMS to EU regions. For higher assurance we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment in your region so nothing crosses boundaries.
[00:05:54] Maya: On RBAC and SSO — we require SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO, and role separation so that only certain service accounts can request wrap/unwrap. How granular is the RBAC?
[00:06:05] Ravi: We provide RBAC at the org, project, and route level. You can restrict key usage to specific service principals, restrict admin operations to security admins, and integrate SAML for SSO plus SCIM for provisioning. We log all role changes and can show audit trails for SCIM events.
[00:06:19] Erin: Legal asks about key escrow and access: we need contractual language that Redwood cannot unilaterally access unwrapped customer keys. Is that part of the standard enterprise contract?
[00:06:29] Jamie: We have BYOK contractual clauses and can include explicit non-access and non-escrow language. For Private deployments there's an additional layer where the customer fully controls the key material and Redwood's control plane can be under the customer's network. We'll follow up with suggested contract language.
[00:06:45] Maya: What about ephemeral keys for model inference? Some of our use cases require short-lived session keys per inference.
[00:06:52] Ravi: We can generate ephemeral DEKs per session using GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext patterns or by using a short TTL on wrapped keys. This reduces blast radius and aligns with zero-trust patterns.
[00:07:05] Luis: Storage encryption of model KV cache — I heard you mention KV cash earlier in another call — what's the risk of key leakage from caches?
[00:07:14] Ravi: We store caches encrypted with DEKs in RAM and optionally at rest with envelope encryption. The DEK lifecycle is short and is never persisted in plaintext on disk. We also provide optional memory encryption and pinning on Dedicated deployments. Sorry for the earlier transcription — KV cash, yes, KV cache.
[00:07:32] Jake: For the audit stream, we want near real-time forwarding to our SIEM with guarantees about delivery ordering. Is that supported?
[00:07:40] Sofia: We can stream events with ordering metadata, and we support retry/backpressure semantics. For very strict guarantees we recommend direct log export to your S3 bucket or Syslog endpoint which you control, combined with event sequence numbers.
[00:07:53] Maya: Regarding HSM vendors — which ones do you commonly support? We use Thales and AWS CloudHSM in parts of the org.
[00:08:02] Ravi: We commonly support AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, Thales/HSM appliances in Private deployments, and integrations with HSM partners. For cloud KMS we rely on provider-managed HSMs (e.g., AWS KMS backed by CloudHSM).
[00:08:15] Luis: Any FIPS or PCI attestations? We have PCI scope in some products.
[00:08:20] Jamie: Our platform supports FIPS-compliant cipher suites, and we can operate in environments that meet PCI requirements. We'll provide relevant attestation docs; for PCI often the customer's environment boundary matters as well.
[00:08:33] Erin: A couple of legal points — record retention and the right to audit. Can Aurora run a security assessment or audit on the deployment?
[00:08:42] Jamie: Enterprise customers can run on-site assessments for Private, and for Hosted/Dedicated we provide SOC2 reports and support vendor security questionnaires. We can provision a virtual security review with our security team and, if necessary, a red-team attestation.
[00:08:55] Maya: You mentioned encryption key lifecycle — does Redwood ever generate root keys for hosted customers?
[00:09:01] Ravi: For hosted customers that opt-in to Redwood-managed keys, we manage CMKs. For BYOK customers, the CMK is customer-managed. We do not generate or keep your master key material in plaintext for BYOK.
[00:09:12] Luis: How do you handle backups and archived artifacts — are those encrypted with the same keys?
[00:09:17] Sofia: Backups are encrypted using the same envelope encryption strategy. We can pin backups to the same region and KMS where required. Archived snapshots can be re-encrypted with rotated keys per policy.
[00:09:29] Jake: On performance — calling KMS on every wrap/unwrap could add latency. Do you have suggested patterns to keep latency low?
[00:09:36] Ravi: Right — per-request KMS calls are expensive. We recommend a hybrid: use GenerateDataKey to create DEKs and cache them in secure memory for short TTLs. For strict compliance, you can do wrap/unwrap on every op, but for low-latency inference we use cached DEKs combined with HSM-backed key origin. We can tune TTLs per route.
[00:09:57] Maya: We also want proof of separation of duties — can you show that platform engineers can't decrypt customer data?
[00:10:04] Jamie: Yes, our internal controls, RBAC, and key management policies enforce separation. Access to decryption workflows is audited and restricted to a small set of ops staff; we can provide an IAM map and proof of the control processes in the SOC2 report.
[00:10:18] Erin: One more legal concern — if we terminate the contract, what's the key destruction and data deletion process?
[00:10:24] Sofia: We have documented data deletion procedures including key zeroization. For BYOK, you control the CMK and can revoke access; for Redwood-managed keys, we can securely destroy key material and provide certification of deletion. We'll include standard termination clauses in the contract.
[00:10:38] Luis: For high security, do you support client-side encryption SDK so we encrypt before sending to Redwood?
[00:10:44] Ravi: Yes, you can do client-side encryption. That shifts more responsibility to Aurora, but it's supported. We can also help with SDK examples for envelope patterns.
[00:10:54] Maya: Okay good. Let's talk about a demo — we want to see the BYOK flow with our AWS KMS key and an HSM-backed scenario.
[00:11:02] Jamie: We'll put together a BYOK demo. Ravi will show GenerateDataKey and wrap/unwrap flows with both cloud KMS and a simulated HSM. We'll include logs export and show how audit events look in SIEM.
[00:11:16] Ravi: For the demo I'll include steps: 1) Register CMK ARN in Redwood, 2) Perform GenerateDataKey and show wrapped DEK storage, 3) Rotate CMK and show rewrap, 4) Stream audit logs to S3 and show event payloads, 5) Show mTLS setup for a Dedicated peering.
[00:11:34] Jake: Can we get an architecture diagram for the Dedicated and Private deployment options showing where keys live?
[00:11:40] Jamie: Yes, we'll send that in the follow-up packet.
[00:11:44] Maya: Any gotchas we should be aware of around latency or throughput when using EKM?
[00:11:50] Ravi: EKM adds network latency and can be a bottleneck; we typically recommend caching DEKs where possible and routing high-throughput routes to Dedicated capacity in region to reduce cross-region hops. For extremely latency-sensitive paths, you might choose to run Private on-prem with local HSMs.
[00:12:06] Luis: About encryption algorithms — do you support AES-GCM, AES-GCM-SIV and RSA for key wrapping?
[00:12:12] Sofia: We support AES-256 GCM for data encryption, and standard key wrap algorithms used by cloud KMS (e.g., AEAD and KMS-managed wrap). We can support alternative algorithms based on customer requirements.
[00:12:22] Erin: From legal I need to confirm retention of audit logs — how long do you retain logs by default, and can we set longer retention?
[00:12:29] Jamie: Default retention is 90 days for high-fidelity logs in the console; we offer extended retention as an add-on and you can export to your S3 for indefinite storage.
[00:12:37] Maya: Great. Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[00:12:40] Jamie: Recap: We'll send SOC2/ISO docs and architecture diagram (Jamie). Ravi will prepare BYOK demo runbook and scripts for both AWS KMS and an HSM scenario. Aurora to share key policy and rotation windows. We'll schedule the follow-up with cloud security + KMS admin in the week of 2026-07-20. Pricing estimate for Dedicated+HSM add-on will be provided.
[00:13:02] Maya: Sounds good. Anything else?
[00:13:05] Erin: No, that's it for legal. Thanks everyone.
[00:13:08] Jamie: Thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and the packet.

[00:13:30] Speaker 1: (brief cross talk, logistics about calendar invites)
[00:15:10] Ravi: (quietly) I'll include example CLI calls: aws kms generate-data-key, then show how the AES-256 DEK is wrapped by the CMK and how Redwood stores only the ciphertext.
[00:18:20] Luis: (asks) Are there open source tools or reference implementations?
[00:18:25] Sofia: We have a GitHub repo with example wrappers and a step-by-step BYOK guide. We'll include links.
[00:22:40] Maya: (notes) We'll want to share our security questionnaire — it's long but important.
[00:22:45] Jamie: We'll fill it out and provide expedited answers for critical sections.
[00:28:10] Ravi: One technical note: when using cloud KMS, we rely on provider rate limits so for very high TPS you should either provision dedicated capacity or use local key caching.
[00:32:05] Jake: For the Private deployment, how does patching and updates work? We need to ensure timely patches but minimal outage windows.
[00:32:12] Sofia: For Private we coordinate patch windows and can offer rolling upgrades with minimal impact; for Dedicated we do rolling pool updates with SLA commitments.
[00:36:50] Maya: That's it from security side, thanks. We'll look for the docs and the demo scheduling.
[00:37:00] Jamie: Thank you, team. We'll follow up with the packet by tomorrow.
[00:48:30] End of recording.

Notes: Transcription contains some small mis-hearings (e.g., KV cash -> KV cache). References to specific product names were kept generic on request. Attachments to be sent: SOC2 PDF, ISO cert, architecture diagram, BYOK runbook link, GitHub examples, pricing slide.
